gate: GPU_PAIR_VECTOR_V1 - Gate A: does the GPU compute every pair's 3-D impulse J = (h*g)*d exactly as the CPU E2? Gate B (only if A passes): does an in-GPU canonical atom reduction give the CPU's per-atom force F endpoint for endpoint?
classification: FORCES ONLY - NO MOMENTUM / POSITION UPDATE, NO KDK, NO TRAJECTORY ON GPU

baseline.this_branch: claude/gpu-pair-vector-v1 in the main checkout (no worktree); clean at start
baseline.frozen_untouched: no G0 file, no existing evidence, no executor, no mpmath file is modified

reference_semantics.cpu_forces: exact_expression_gate_v1.stream.run's forces(q, step) with the E2 force (rw:R1+R2 at iv.prec = p), non-exact path: for (i, j) in canonical order (i < j, lexicographic): d[k] = q[j][k] - q[i][k]; r2 = (d0*d0 + d1*d1) + d2*d2; st = K.domain(r2) (PROVEN if lo >= R_MIN2, VIOLATED if hi < R_MIN2, else UNPROVEN; exact rational comparison) - not PROVEN raises DomainStop(st, step); g = G(r2); for k in 0, 1, 2: t = (h*g)*d[k] (h*g recomputed per k as in the source); F[j][k] = F[j][k] + t; F[i][k] = F[i][k] - t; F starts at the lifted 0
reference_semantics.every_operation: mpmath 1.3.0 interval arithmetic (mpi_sub, mpi_mul incl. sign cases, mpi_add) - replicated on the GPU with the G0 device arithmetic (g0.cu, included verbatim); G(R^2) by the G0 traced program; G0's exp is a replica of mpmath's integer algorithm, not a correctly rounded exp, and the same holds here
reference_semantics.not_the_same: (h*g)*d is not h*(g*d); the order of additions into F[a][k] is the canonical pair order and is not commutative for intervals

gate_A.gpu: input: the N x 3 position intervals of one state (exact dyadic words); device: canonical pair table (i, j) by pair id; kernel 1 per pair: d, r2, domain status (exact comparison with R_MIN2 = a / b, uploaded as integers); kernel 2 per pair: G (G0 program interpreter, only for PROVEN pairs); kernel 3 per pair: J[k] = (h*g)*d[k], each k computing h*g as the source does; output per pair: status, pair id echo, obligation mask, device precision echo, r2, G, J0, J1, J2

classes.PAIR_EXACT: domain status equal and all 6 endpoints of J equal
classes.PAIR_SOUND_ONLY: status equal, every component contains the CPU interval, some endpoint differs
classes.PAIR_UNSOUND: some component does not contain the CPU interval

gate_A.pass: PAIR_UNSOUND = 0, DOMAIN_MISMATCH = 0, no missing / reordered pair, all layouts identical; target PAIR_EXACT 100 %. If EXACT breaks, the cause is investigated before any performance number is used
gate_A.A1_correctness_path: all pair outputs (incl. r2 and G) copied back and decoded
gate_A.A2_performance_path: host position encode, H2D, kernel d/r2, kernel G, kernel J, D2H of J records, host decode (+ the host canonical reduction of the decoded J to F, reported separately) - CUDA events between the three kernels

gate_B.start_condition: only if gate A passes on the whole sample bundle

alternatives_compared_before_implementat.B1_store_then_reduce: J of every pair stays in GPU memory (O(N^2)); one thread per (atom a, component k) adds, in canonical pair order, +J for the pairs (i, a), i < a, then -J for the pairs (a, j), j > a (this is exactly the order in which the CPU loop touches F[a][k]). G and J are computed once per pair. Device memory per pair: d 3 x 88 B + r2 88 + G 88 + J record 16 + 3 x 88 + debug copy 176 = 896 B
alternatives_compared_before_implementat.B2_recompute_per_atom: one thread per atom recomputes d, r2, G, J for its N-1 pairs in canonical order and accumulates directly: O(N) memory, but every pair's G (the dominant cost, ~5-7 ms per thread on the GPU in G0) is computed twice and the per-atom thread does N-1 G evaluations serially (N = 64: 63 sequential G per thread vs 1 in B1) - the kernel latency grows ~N times
alternatives_compared_before_implementat.choice: B1: simpler to verify (the pair results are the exact gate-A results already checked), one G per pair, O(N^2) memory is small for the target sizes (estimates below). B2 is not implemented in V1

gate_B.gpu: kernel 4 (B1): thread per (a, k) over the pre-computed J buffer in the order above; F starts as the exact interval 0; F = mpi_add(F, J) when a is j, F = mpi_sub(F, J) when a is i; no atomics, no tree, no partial sums; output per (a, k): F interval with atom and component echo; only N x 3 intervals are copied back
gate_B.domain_stop: if any pair of the state is not PROVEN the CPU raises DomainStop at the first such pair; the GPU reports the first non-PROVEN pair id and kind (the host scans statuses in canonical order) and F is not used
gate_B.pass: 100 % endpoint equality of every F[a][k] with the CPU reduction; any difference = B_FAIL

sample_bundle.states: the same four trajectories as G0 (N = 40, 64 at T = 100, p = 109; N = 12, 16 at T = 1000, p = 163) at steps 0, T/10, T/2, T: the exact position intervals q passed to forces(q, step) and the force F that call returned, recorded from a run of stream.run's own source with one inserted observer line before 'return F' (built at runtime from inspect.getsource; no file changed); every run must end equal to its verified V2 Vast serial reference, else no bundle
sample_bundle.test_only: domain probe states (N = 3 positions chosen so that one pair is VIOLATED, one UNPROVEN) at p = 109 and 163, with their CPU statuses; and p = 128 / 192 replays of the N = 40 step-50 state (positions re-used, CPU F recomputed at that p)
sample_bundle.encoding: G0 dyadic encoding (sign, odd mantissa hex, binary exponent, bitcount); positions echoed by the device and compared exactly
sample_bundle.seal: bundle + sha256 committed before any GPU code of this stage

checker: independent: imports none of this stage's GPU host / CUDA code and none of G0's GPU code; with its own literal forces loop (mpmath iv, frozen RwForce, K.domain, K.H) recomputes d, r2, G, J for every pair and F for every state; its F must equal the F recorded from the real run (validates the checker's loop); compares statuses, pair identity and order (id echo), position echo, precision echo, all J and F endpoints, obligation masks, and all layouts bit for bit
layouts: every bundle state with block 32, 64, 128, 256 and grid 1, 7, ceil(n / block) for all kernels (12 layouts); every output byte identical

performance.official_host: Vast 52763685 (Threadripper PRO 3975WX + RTX 3090; the designer starts it on request); any host change = amendment before the run; desktop RTX 4060 = correctness cross-check only

paths.CPU_W6_E2: the validated E2 pair path: six unchanged e2_pair_parallel_v1.run._pair_worker processes (pinned 1,2,3,4,5,0, main on 0) receive the positions, return (status, J) for their contiguous canonical blocks; the main reduces in canonical order exactly as run_parallel's forces does; timed per state (one force evaluation)
paths.GPU_A_PAIR_VECTOR: encode positions, H2D, 3 kernels, D2H of P x 3 J, decode; plus a host canonical reduction to F (separate number)
paths.GPU_B_ATOM_REDUCE: encode positions, H2D, 4 kernels, D2H of N x 3 F, decode

combinations (sealed; information value.state: FCC_N initial state (step 0, lifted at p)
FCC_N initial state (step 0, lifted at p)
FCC_N initial state (step 0, lifted at p): the p effect at the same N

performance.repetitions: GPU warm median of 5 (first call per size discarded), cold once per p in a fresh process; CPU_W6 median of 3 after spawn
performance.resource_sweep: after correctness only: block 32, 64, 128, 256 (grid = ceil) for N = 64 and N = 128 at p = 109; outputs must be identical; recorded, no rule changed
performance.cost_estimate: GPU per state ~10-30 ms; CPU_W6 per state ~0.1 s (N = 40) to ~1.5 s (N = 128); total campaign well under 15 min on the host
performance.memory: exact allocated bytes per N (pair table, d, r2, G, J records, debug copies, atom output, positions) recorded, plus a computed table for N = 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024

gpu_execution_plan_record: every run stores a GpuExecutionPlan {block_size, grid_blocks, batch_size (= pair count), pair_storage_mode, atom_reduction_mode, precision} with wall, per-kernel times, encode, decode, memory and correctness - data only, no learning
fault_injections: 3 dz component of J not written (device)
6 K.domain check removed (device; detected on the domain probe states)
10 atom reduction order changed: (a, j) pairs before (i, a) pairs (device)
11 layout-dependent (unordered) reduction order: start rotated by block index (device)
13 p altered: the program uploaded at p = 128 for a p = 109 state (host)
14 device overflow treated as success (reduced work limbs with the poison check off, as G0 fault 8)

decision_rules_sealed.A_FAIL: any PAIR_UNSOUND or PAIR_SOUND_ONLY left unexplained, DOMAIN_MISMATCH, missing / reordered pair, or a layout difference in gate A
decision_rules_sealed.B_FAIL: gate A exact but some F endpoint differs
decision_rules_sealed.A_EXACT_B_BOTTLENECK: gate A exact, gate B not yet run or failed for reasons outside correctness, and the pair-vector path is dominated by encode / decode / output volume
decision_rules_sealed.B_EXACT_NOT_FASTER: A and B exact, but GPU_B total is not clearly faster than CPU_W6 at N = 40 and 64
decision_rules_sealed.GPU_PAIR_PROMISING: A exact, B exact, layout independent, no silent overflow, and GPU_B total (encode + transfers + kernels + decode) <= 0.5 x CPU_W6 at both N = 40 and N = 64 (p = 109)
decision_rules_sealed.next_if_promising: GPU_ONE_STEP_V1 (one full KDK step compared CPU vs GPU) - not started here

claims_forbidden: bit identity on the samples is a proof
kernel time alone is GPU speed
